label: STOPP C6: ticlopidine
title: Ticlopidine
statement: Ticlopidine in any circumstances (clopidogrel and prasugrel have similar efficacy, stronger evidence and fewer side-effects).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y
source.credit: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: Ticlopidine carries serious adverse effects. If the patient still takes it, review the indication and which antiplatelet is suitable. Prasugrel is contraindicated after a stroke or transient ischaemic attack.

medicine_groups.name: Ticlopidine
medicine_groups.note: Tilodene and Ticlid are ticlopidine tablets. Ticlid may appear on an overseas history. Clopidogrel and prasugrel are not in this group.

rule_for_models: Apply this criterion only to people aged 65 or older. If age is under 65, there is no finding. If age is unknown, request the age before confirming a finding. Suspect a finding when ticlopidine (Group A) appears anywhere in the history, in any circumstances. One supply is enough.
cannot_be_seen: Why ticlopidine was supplied, and whether it came from overseas or a compounding source. Also whether another antiplatelet is taken as well.
ask_the_gp: Whether ticlopidine can be changed to clopidogrel or another suitable antiplatelet.
